messages:
Sam (support): FYI receiving p99 timeouts from ACME tenant since ~12:30UTC, customer says requests randomly hang and then 504. they attached a session id.
Priya (eng-sre): Can you paste the session id + a quick repro? also linking grafana for that cluster: http://grafana.internal/d/ingress?var=pool=gp2
Sam (support): session=acme-9f3a; repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","prompt":"small"}' — intermittently >10s then 504
Maya (customer-success): Customer notes p95 is OK but p99 jumps a lot, and it's only for their tenant. No billing errors.
Priya (eng-sre): Looking at ingress traces — spikes line up with large batch jobs from other tenants hitting the same pool. Admission metrics show long queue depth and fairness skewed.
Priya (eng-sre): Logs:
```
2026-03-17T12:31:02Z admit_controller: tenant=acme queue_ms=4100 admit=queued
2026-03-17T12:31:05Z worker: batch.size=128 delay_ms=1200 processed
2026-03-17T12:31:06Z request: tenant=acme deadline_exceeded
```
Luca (eng-platform): Sounds like per-tenant concurrency cap is not enforced when large batchers occupy worker slots. Could be admission tokens being drained by long-running batched requests.
Sam (support): Customer wants an ETA — can we do a quick mitigation?
Luca (eng-platform): Short term: 1) reduce max_batch_size on gp2 pool from 128 -> 64, 2) lower batch_wait_ms from 50 -> 20, 3) enable per-tenant queue weights for acme (higher weight). That should free slots for small low-latency queries.
Priya (eng-sre): I'll flip batch_wait on gp2 in the next 2 min. If we still see issues, we can pin acme into a dedicated burst pool.
Priya (eng-sre): Command I'm running: `infractl pool update gp2 --max-batch-size=64 --batch-wait-ms=20` — rolling change to workers.
oncall-bot: change accepted, starting rollout to 24 nodes (eta ~90s)
Priya (eng-sre): Rollout finished. Early telemetry: queue depth down 60%, p99 for acme dropped from 1.2s -> 220ms on initial samples.
Sam (support): Confirmed with customer, they're seeing big improvement. They still saw one 1.5s outlier ~a minute ago.
Luca (eng-platform): Follow-ups: schedule RFC to add per-route fairness enforcement and a fast-path for small requests (bypass large-batch workers). Also add an alert when queue depth disparity between tenants > 3x.
Maya (customer-success): I'll update the customer and propose a dedicated burst pool if they scale. 
Priya (eng-sre): Filing post-incident note + action items. Ticket: INC-4523. Assigning Luca to RFC. :white_check_mark:
